name: mage-workbench
description: Browser-native modeling workbench for MAGE model systems. Pure client-side: no server, no account, no install.
// why engines: The FLOOR, not the pin, and the two are deliberately separate. `engines.node` is the oldest Node that works: 22, because the gates load .ts entry points directly (Node strips types from 22 onward) and because html-validate 11.x calls fs.globSync, added in 22. The PIN — what `nvm use` selects and what CI installs via `node-version-file: .nvmrc` — lives in .nvmrc at the repo root and says 24. Collapsing them would delete a distinction the publishing workflow uses; copying either number anywhere else would be a second source of truth. `npm run check:node` reads BOTH from their own files and asserts the pin satisfies the floor. Note that npm does not enforce this field without engine-strict, so the preflight is the enforcement and this is the declaration.

scripts.types: json2ts -i mage-model.schema.json -o src/ir/schema-model.ts --additionalProperties false && json2ts -i mage-query.schema.json -o src/ir/schema-query.ts --additionalProperties false && json2ts -i mage-transaction.schema.json -o src/ir/schema-transaction.ts --additionalProperties false
scripts.all: npm run check:node && npm run check && npm run check:parity && npm run test && npm run build && npm run test:smoke

// why --test-timeout on the browser tie: These tiers hold real Chromiums, and a test wedged mid-flight used to hang the whole tier (and the pre-push gate) at zero CPU, forever — the 261006 incidents. 300s bounds each test AND each file wrapper, so a wedge becomes a cancelled-test red inside five minutes instead of a silent infinite stall. The whole tier runs in ~25s on an idle machine, so the ceiling has an order of magnitude of headroom for a loaded one; the harness's leak watchdog covers the sibling failure (tests pass but a leaked handle blocks process exit), which no per-test timeout can see. The node tier has no browsers and keeps the runner default.
// why the pre hooks: npm runs a `pre<name>` script automatically, which is the only Node wiring here that does not depend on someone remembering it — and a gate you have to remember is what the 261003 failures walked past. Every gate above either loads a .ts entry point or imports one (build.mjs does), so each dies under Node 20 with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION: a module-load TypeError that reads like broken code. The preflight costs ~30ms and runs first, so the failure says WRONG NODE and names the fix instead. `check` is wired too, even though tsc runs anywhere: someone on the wrong Node should learn it from the first gate they run rather than the third.
